geometry_edits.rationale: Wrap the hall in a new courtyard/entry-void macro to make the access edge more legible while keeping the protected hall node in ancestry.
Use a modest carve so the building remains a dominant hall rather than turning into fragmented bars.
Promote the new courtyard-wrapped composition as the root so the hall remains in ancestry and the public void becomes part of the executable geometry.

graph_edits.rationale: Introduce a carved public court/entry void to strengthen the ground response and gymnasium threshold logic while preserving the dominant hall ancestry.
Keep the courtyard cut shallow enough to preserve the long-span hall as the dominant mass and avoid over-fragmentation.
Shift the roof/section language toward a clearer daylight-monitor hall logic, aligning better with the gymnasium roof invariant.
Preserve the long-span reading along the existing horizontal axis so the dominant gesture remains intact.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent long, low mass across all four views, so it avoids the common failure of being coherent in only one projection. The dominant gesture is legible and the roof section clearly expresses a continuous spanning datum rather than a random sculptural stack. The stepped/ribbed condition is relatively coherent and does not feel like code-minimum setbacks. However, the ground response is weak: there is almost no meaningful public void, court, undercut, or entry seam visible, which is a major miss for a gymnasium brief that asks for a subordinate entry/service hierarchy and an accessible public edge. The mass is also somewhat sealed and generic in its rectangularity, so while it can plausibly support a gym hall, it needs a stronger carved access/void condition to better satisfy the program contract. The overall form is closer to a disciplined hall-bar than a courtyard building; that is acceptable for the hard pass, but it should be improved with a legible public cut or undercut at the frontage.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Long, low sports bar with a clear roof datum and public-facing edge; supports the idea of a readable hall under a continuous section.

warnings: No visible parcel boundary or road frontage was provided in the candidate image, so site-response scoring is limited to the internal massing logic.
Void/publicness is the weakest aspect; the form currently reads more as a sealed hall bar than as an entry-responsive sports building.
